title: Second Shift
tagline: A 60-year-old bakery in a city that never sleeps.

facts.fed_kid: Arjun waits by the back door.
facts.met_chain: You met with the chain bakery.

cards.speaker: The back door
cards.text: 3 a.m. A teenager asks for yesterday's bread. Mr. Rao, the owner, sells it in the morning at half price.

a.label: Give it free
a.result: He takes the loaf like it might vanish. "Thanks," he says, already half gone.
a.later: The kid, Arjun, now waits by the back door every night. He's started sweeping up.

b.label: Point to the sign
b.result: He reads it twice, then leaves without a word.
b.later: The kid never came back. You catch yourself looking for him.

cards.speaker: Gloria
cards.text: Your sourdough starter, Gloria, smells off.

a.label: Nurse her for three days
a.result: You feed her carefully, discard carefully, wait.
a.later: Gloria came back stronger. The crust has never been better.

b.label: Start fresh
b.result: You wash the jar. Something ends with the rinse water.
b.later: The new starter is fine. Mr. Rao says the bread tastes 'polite'.

cards.speaker: The flour store
cards.text: A rat in the flour store. Mr. Rao is asleep upstairs.

a.label: Wake him
a.result: He comes down in slippers, already assessing the damage.
a.later: Mr. Rao now trusts you with the spare keys.

b.label: Handle it yourself
b.result: You deal with it quietly. Two sacks don't make it.
b.later: You threw out two sacks. Mr. Rao never found out.

cards.speaker: A recruiter
cards.text: A chain bakery offers you head baker, double pay, starting Monday.

a.label: Take the meeting
a.result: You say you'll listen. The call ends with a calendar invite.
a.later: Word got back to Mr. Rao. He hasn't mentioned it, which is worse.

b.label: Turn it down
b.result: You hang up before they finish the pitch.
b.later: Mr. Rao gave you a raise he couldn't afford.

cards.speaker: Arjun
cards.text: Arjun asks if he can learn to bake.

a.label: Teach him
a.result: You hand him an apron two sizes too big.
a.later: Arjun's first loaf was terrible. His third sold out.

b.label: Not now
b.result: He nods like he expected it. The broom still moves.
b.later: Arjun got a job at the chain bakery across the street.

cards.speaker: The front window
cards.text: A food blogger posts your cardamom bun. A line forms at 5 a.m.

a.label: Bake double, sleep less
a.result: Flour dusts every surface. Dawn arrives without you noticing.
a.later: You made a month's rent in a week and slept through two Sundays.

b.label: Sell out and close early
b.result: You flip the sign while people are still hoping.
b.later: 'Sold out by 8' became the bakery's legend.

cards.speaker: Mr. Rao
cards.text: Mr. Rao asks if you'd ever want to own the place.

a.label: Say yes
a.result: He smiles like he'd been waiting for that word.
a.later: The papers are drawn up. He keeps calling the second oven 'yours'.

b.label: Say you're not sure
b.result: He looks at the floor, then the ovens, then you.
b.later: He nodded and started talking to his nephew instead.

endings.text: The sign gets repainted with two names on it.
The chain buys the bakery and makes you its face. The bread is fine. It isn't yours.
You still bake at 3 a.m. The city still doesn't sleep. Some nights that's enough.
